title: C482/262/2008 of VINOD KUMAR TANDON AND ANOTHER Vs BAHADUR LAL GUPTA

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
CRIMINAL MISCELLANEOUS APPLICATION No. 262/2008
(Under Section 482 of the CrPC)
Vinod Kumar Tandon & Another ÖÖ.Applicants
Versus
Bahadur Lal Gupta ÖÖRespondent
28th June, 2012
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 None has turned up on behalf of the private
opposite party despite sufficient service. So, this Court
rendered hearing to Mr. Pradeep Kumar Chauhan,
Advocate, for the applicants. Also perused the papers on
record.
2. Matter pertains to breach of agreement, which
was executed on a stamp paper of rupees hundred between
the applicants petitioners and the private opposite party,
though it was unregistered one. As per the terms of
agreement, Mr. Vinod Kumar Tandon & his wife Smt.
Sunita Tandon (petitioners) agreed to sell a small piece of
land ad measuring 117.56 square meter located in Khasra
No. 98, Subhash Nagar, Jwalapur, Haridwar to Mr.
Bahadur Lal Gupta (opposite party). Out of the total sale
consideration of ` 9,17,000/-, Mr. Gupta paid ` 2,00,000/-
to the petitioners, as advance, at the time executing the said
agreement. Balance amount of ` 7,17,000/- was to be paid
by him at the time of execution of sale deed, which was
scheduled on 25.8.2007.
3. It is alleged that on 25.8.2007, Mr. Gupta
reached at the office of Registrar for execution of the sale
deed, but the petitioners Mr. & Mrs. Tandon did not turn up

2
till evening. So, Mr. Gupta along with his son Kanhaiyya
Lal, his friend Kunwar Pal and one more person went to the
house of petitioners in the evening of 28.8.2007 and asked
them to execute the sale deed. But Mr. Tandon allegedly
lashed out over Mr. Gupta and also refused to return the
advance money. So, the impugned complaint was filed on
7.9.2007.
4. Learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Haridwar,
after recording the statement of Mr. Gupta under Section
200 CrPC and his witnesses Mr. Kunwar Pal and Kanhaiyya
Lal under Section 202 CrPC, passed the impugned order of
cognizance dated 10.10.2007 and summoned the applicants
petitioners to stand trial for the offences under Section 323,
504, 506, 420, 406 IPC. Hence, this petition.
5. Having gone through the contents of the
complaint and the other materials on record, it is
abundantly clear that the dispute between the parties is
purely civil in nature. If the execution of sale deed was
denied by the petitioners, then the complainant has the
remedy of filing a suit for specific performance of contract.
Allegations made in the compliant prima facie appear to be
colourful, and the complainant has dragged the applicants
petitioners in criminal case in order to harass and put
undue pressure on them. It is an abuse of the process of
court and, therefore, this Court is not inclined to permit the
impugned litigation initiated by the complainant Mr.
Bahadur Lal Gupta against the applicants petitioners.
6. Consequently, petition is allowed. Impugned
order of cognizance dated 10.10.2007, passed by the Chief
Judicial Magistrate, Haridwar and the entire proceedings of

3
Criminal Complaint Case No. 4691/2007, Bahadur Lal
Gupta v. Vinod Kumar Tandon & Another, are hereby
quashed.
7. Registry is directed to inform the court concerned
accordingly.
(Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
28.6.2012
Prabodh
